A 2017 graduate of Bentley University, Mr. Prithvi quickly demonstrated his strategic acumen upon entering the professional arena. His exceptional foresight and leadership were notably displayed when he successfully orchestrated a major collaboration with boAt, India’s leading audio product company, resulting in the production of innovative twin wireless speakers. Mr. Prithvi has been at the forefront of Dixon’s ambitious expansion, spearheading the establishment of a state-of-the-art facility in Chennai. Through strategic partnerships with industry giants like Asus and HP, he has driven the rapid growth of Dixon’s IT hardware division, solidifying its position as a key player in the tech manufacturing landscape.

A proponent of continuous learning and global perspectives, Mr. Prithvi pursued a Master of Business Administration at the prestigious London Business School. Equipped with this advanced degree, he has played a pivotal role in Dixon’s mobile division, managing key accounts such as Jio and Xiaomi. His strategic insights and hands-on leadership have been instrumental in building strong partnerships and significantly contributing to the company’s success. Mr. Prithvi is committed to positioning Dixon Technologies as an engineering powerhouse. He is leading efforts to diversify into new product categories, ensuring that the company remains at the forefront of innovation and continues to scale new heights in the rapidly evolving tech industry.

obj.headline: Management exhibits mixed reliability, lowering revenue guidance while maintaining operating margin commitments and expanding historical profits.

points.text: Management continuously lowered FY27 revenue growth guidance from 1.5-3.5% down to 1.0-2.0%, while dropping effective tax rate and Financial Services growth targets entirely.
Operating margin targets for FY27 (20.0-22.0%) remain on track at an actual 21.03% EBIT margin so far, supported by stable recent quarterly margins.
Multiple operational targets, including Q3FY26 AI revenue contribution and hiring commitments for college grads and Frontier Engineers, remain unverifiable due to missing reporting.
Long-term financials demonstrate strong operational expansion, with annual revenues reaching ₹178,650 crore and PAT growing to ₹29,474 crore in Mar 2026.

bull.text: FY27 operating margin guidance of 20.0-22.0% is on track with 21.03% EBIT margin achieved through 2 quarters.
Strong financial position marked by 40.0% ROCE, low debt-to-equity of 0.09, and Mar 2026 CFO of ₹33,986 crore.
Consistent annual top-line and net profit expansion, with Mar 2026 PAT climbing to ₹29,474 crore.

bear.text: Management repeatedly reduced FY27 revenue growth guidance from 1.5-3.5% down to 1.0-2.0% by Oct 2026.
Key promises regarding effective tax rates and segment growth directions were quietly dropped from recent earnings calls.
Working capital efficiency worsened, with debtor days and cash conversion cycle both rising from 63 to 72 days.

obj.headline: Management is failing to deliver on growth promises amid dropping medium-term targets and compressed margins.

points.text: FY27 revenue growth is off-track at 7.6% across two quarters against a promised 30% target.
Management dropped multiple strategic targets, including FY27/mid-term EBITDA margins, solutions business transition timelines, carbon footprint goals, and 60% solutions revenue share.
Operating margins contracted significantly, dropping from 21.1% in Mar 2025 down to 15.8% in Sep 2026.
Despite margin pressures, annual revenue grew consistently from ₹2,036 crore in Mar 2021 to ₹6,455 crore in Mar 2026.

bull.text: Cash generation remains strong with CFO/PAT ratios above 1.65x over the last 3 years, reaching ₹1,195 crore in Mar 2026.
The balance sheet maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.21 with ROCE at a healthy 26.0% as of Sep 2026.

bear.text: FY27 growth outlook is off-track at just 7.6% actual revenue growth reported so far against a 30% promise.
Annual PAT dropped from ₹840 crore in Mar 2025 to ₹637 crore in Mar 2026 as operating margins declined.

obj.headline: Management dropped key margin guidance promises despite strong revenue growth and improving operating metrics.

points.text: Management abandoned its 11-13% long-term and 12-14% near-to-mid term company-wide EBITDA margin guidance after dropping them from earnings calls.
